extracted.intended_audience: Support Directorate and Agency managers/staff responsible for implementing OMB Circular A-44 (management improvement and reports/records management)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Support Directorate staff on implementing the Management Improvement Program (OMB Circular A-44), with emphasis on reports management, information processing systems, records microfilming, and achieving cost-reduction quotas. Covers inventorying reports, assessing report value, system design activity, and pilot projects for microform applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rendering staff assistance on Agency and Directorate-wide programs
rubrics_metrics.description: "our only input to the Management Improvement Program can b4 by rendering staff assistance on Agency and Directorate wide programs (i.e. Reports Management program which is a part of 0MB Circular A-44)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit reporting to own Staff budget and managerial control; contribute by providing staff assistance (coordination, proposals, development) rather than by direct budgeted programs when primary issues are Directorate/Agency-wide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate Reports Management Program and develop new information processing concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: "This we are doing by coordinating the DD/S Reports Management Program and developing new concepts and proposals for managing Information Processing activities in the Support Directorate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide coordination across offices for reports management and produce proposals for new approaches in information processing; proposals may be elevated for annual program consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information processing systems design, testing and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Information Processing Branch of SSS continues its work in design, testing and implementation of various information processing system areas. At present, there are ten major systems under design and these major systems are further subdivided into 41 subsystems or projects."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track scope (# major systems and subsystems), progress in design/testing/implementation, and manage projects as discrete subsystems to control and measure work; document system areas and project breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess the value and need for centrally prepared management information reports
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Support Directorate has responsibility for assessing the value and need for regulatory and other centrally prepared management information reports produced by or for offices of the Support Directorate and disseminated throughout the Agency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each report for value and necessity (regulatory or management function), identify redundant or low-value reports, and recommend retention, consolidation, or elimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete reports inventory and cost accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: "A reports inventory has been completed identifying 1600 management information reports in the DDS, and with an overall cost of $1,636,000."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a comprehensive inventory with report counts and attached cost estimates; use inventory data to target reductions and justify program changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achieve assigned cost-reduction goal and quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: "The cost reduction goal for FY 1972 established by O/PPB for the Support Directorate is a 7.5% reduction of approximately $125,000. Quotas have been assigned to various Support Offices and Support Services Staff will provide assistance in developing a continuing reports management program to meet these goals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate overall percentage targets into office-level quotas; provide assistance for offices to meet quotas via report elimination/consolidation or efficiency gains; monitor progress against monetary targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey records for potential microform (microfilming) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: "Survey of records for potential microform applications. ... there have been studies and much discussion about the development of a program for microfilming Agency records as a means of getting some relief for critical space problems ... a recently completed study suggests that it may be cost effective to microfilm certain collections of records for the primary purpose of conserving storage space, provided that certain criteria can be met in the collection of files to microfilm."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume microfilming justified solely for space savings; apply pre-established selection criteria to identify candidate record collections; consider expert consensus and study findings when deciding applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct detailed cost-benefit analyses for selected record collections
rubrics_metrics.description: "We are now undertaking a detailed cost benefit analysis of a few carefully selected ... collections of records. This analysis involves the identification of record collections in Support Directorate offices which meet as many as possible of the pre-established criteria."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each candidate collection, perform a thorough cost-benefit study considering preservation, access needs, storage savings, and conversion costs; prefer pilotable collections that meet multiple criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review survey results for broader system implications and feasibility; run pilot filming projects
rubrics_metrics.description: "Representatives of the Support Services Staff and the Printing Services Division, OL, will review information collected in this survey in terms of broader system implications as well as the feasibility of treating them as individual applications. Additional data will be developed as required ... We expect to mount two or three pilot filming projects within the next six months."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate candidate microfilming projects both as isolated applications and for their implications on records/printing systems; develop additional data where needed; implement 2–3 pilots to validate assumptions and cost-effectiveness before wider rollout.
